Farm visit: BAF Agriculture (part 2) – A brand new grow-finisher farm

Part 1 of this 3-part series explained how the Vietnamese pig integrator BAF Agriculture managed to grow in a market that loves pork, yet operates in difficult circumstances due to the presence of pig pathogens like African Swine Fever. This year, it opened Tay An Khanh farm.

Vincent ter BeekEditor of Pig Progress / Topic: Pigs around the world

Aug 5

Article

The first piglets had already entered the weaner house. Photo: BAF Agriculture

READ PART 1

Tay An Khanh farm is a complex of 16 pig houses, which measures 888 by 542 m. Four of the buildings are in use for weaner pigs and 12 are home to finishers, being the majority of the buildings. The finisher houses altogether provide space in 68 rooms for finishers, with 14 pens on either side of a central aisle. Each fully slatted pen measures 6.5 m x 2.4 m. That way, every finisher room measures 490 m2 for 670 animals in total. The weaner houses look fairly well set up – there are 32 rooms with 24 pens per room.

Outside view of the finisher pig houses at Tay An Khanh farm. - Photo: Vincent ter Beek

At the time of the visit, weaned piglets had already arrived in different buildings of the complex, which was temporarily fenced off to segregate between the areas with high biosecurity – and those without. In the area without pigs, helmeted workers are busy doing final checks. Behind the fences, however, a completely different regime applied.

Aerial picture of Tay An Khanh pig farm. Photo: BAF Agriculture

On-site team

What will eventually apply to the entire farm is a regime in which the total facility will be serviced by a team living on-site in a dormitory, which is a separate zone within the farm premises, equipped with playgrounds, housing and leisure facilities. Once an employee enters the farm, he or she will continue to stay there for 6 to 8 weeks before heading out again. In order to enter the farm premises on his/her way to the dormitory area, a shower is required, after which he or she needs to test negative for ASF virus. To get close to the pigs, two more showers are required, explains Duy. A first additional shower will be required to formally enter the zone of the pig houses, a second is required to enter each individual building.

Set-up of the finisher houses, with 14 pens on either side of the aisle. Photo: Vincent ter Beek

On the far end of the farm is a facility for wastewater treatment. After treatment, the liquid part will be used as fertiliser for its own crops. The farm also features solar panels and a biogas installation. This has a separate entrance and a separate dormitory. Staff working there have their own regime and will not get to the pigs themselves.

A narrow corridor separates layers 2 and 3 of the filtration system. Photo: Vincent ter Beek

Interestingly, BAF Agriculture promotes its pork as being from ‘100% vegetarian-fed pigs’. It is a message that finds resonance with the Vietnamese audience as the pork is perceived to be delicious, explain the company representatives. As a result, BAF Agriculture refrains from using animal-derived ingredients. All in all, the farm feeds 7 different proprietary diets from suckling to finishing.

One washing station for the entire southern cluster

Since 2025, the southern cluster of BAF Agriculture has operated a 2-stop truck washing station. Every empty pig or feed truck that is driving to or from one of the BAF pig farms will have to drive through this location. A first component of the washing station consists of a wet treatment – three trucks can be treated simultaneously. A truck simply has to be parked and then by using a remote control, a programme can be started. Spraying devices are running on rails underneath as well as on top of the truck, giving the trucks a rinse with a mixture of water and a disinfectant. Cleaning the inside of the trucks is happening manually in a separate room.

The next component consists of a 30-minute dry treatment, in which every truck is dried with hot air to a temperature of 65°C – a temperature at which many viruses, including ASF virus, are thought not to be able to survive. For truck drivers, there is the possibility to get refreshments or even have a snooze in case the full washing treatment takes a few hours. Full feed trucks will get another manual cleaning treatment before entering any farm’s outer perimeter.

A spraying device on a rail, cleaning trucks from underneath. Photo: Vincent ter Beek

A freshly washed pig truck, ready to pick up piglets at one of BAF Agriculture’s farms.

translationZh:
本系列文章的第1部分介绍了越南养猪整合商BAF农业如何在喜爱猪肉却因非洲猪瘟等病原体而面临困难的市场中实现增长。今年，该公司开设了Tay An Khanh农场。

Tay An Khanh农场是一个由16栋猪舍组成的综合体，占地888米×542米。其中4栋用于保育猪，12栋用于育肥猪，占建筑的大多数。育肥舍总共提供68个房间，每个房间中央过道两侧各有14个栏位。每个全漏缝地板栏位尺寸为6.5米×2.4米。这样，每个育肥房间面积为490平方米，共饲养670头猪。保育舍设置得相当完善——有32个房间，每间24个栏位。

参观时，断奶仔猪已经进入综合体的不同建筑，该综合体暂时用围栏隔开，以区分高生物安全区域和非高生物安全区域。在没有猪的区域，戴着安全帽的工人正忙着进行最后检查。然而，在围栏后面，实行的是完全不同的制度。

**现场团队**

最终将适用于整个农场的制度是：整个设施将由一个住在现场宿舍区的团队服务，宿舍区是农场内的一个独立区域，配备游乐场、住房和休闲设施。员工一旦进入农场，将在那里继续停留6至8周，然后才离开。为了进入农场前往宿舍区，需要淋浴，之后必须检测非洲猪瘟病毒阴性。Duy解释说，要接近猪只，还需要再淋浴两次。第一次额外淋浴是正式进入猪舍区域，第二次是进入每栋建筑。

农场远端是废水处理设施。处理后，液体部分将用作自家作物的肥料。农场还配备了太阳能电池板和沼气装置。该设施有单独的入口和单独的宿舍。在那里工作的员工有自己的制度，不会接触猪只。

有趣的是，BAF农业宣传其猪肉来自“100%素食喂养的猪”。公司代表解释说，这一信息引起了越南消费者的共鸣，因为他们认为这种猪肉味道鲜美。因此，BAF农业避免使用动物源性成分。总的来说，农场从哺乳期到育肥期共饲喂7种不同的自配日粮。

**南部集群的一个清洗站**

自2025年起，BAF农业南部集群运营了一个两站式卡车清洗站。每辆空载猪只或饲料卡车在往返于BAF猪场之间时，都必须经过该地点。清洗站的第一个组成部分是湿处理——三辆卡车可以同时处理。卡车只需停放，然后通过遥控器启动程序。喷洒装置在卡车下方和上方的轨道上运行，用水和消毒剂的混合物冲洗卡车。卡车内部的清洁在单独的房间里手动进行。

下一个组成部分是30分钟的干燥处理，每辆卡车用65°C的热风干燥——在这个温度下，许多病毒，包括非洲猪瘟病毒，被认为无法存活。对于卡车司机，如果整个清洗过程需要几个小时，他们可以享用茶点甚至小睡片刻。满载饲料的卡车在进入任何农场外围之前，将接受另一次手动清洁处理。
author: Vincent ter Beek
